title: Lexical Analysis With Flex: Introduction
why: Documents regular-expression rules and generated C scanner source.

title: Lexical Analysis With Flex: Options for Scanner Speed and Size
why: Documents scanner tables and their default compression.

title: Lexer (The GNU C Preprocessor Internals)
why: Describes GCC's hand-coded lexer and its positioning and contextual-token requirements.

title: ISO/IEC 9899:201x Committee Draft N1570 (HTML transcription)
why: Readable transcription of the primary C committee draft, including postfix increment and decrement constraints and semantics.

claim: By default flex generates a C source file defining yylex.
quote: flex generates as output a C source file, lex.yy.c by default, which defines a routine yylex().

locator: Options for Scanner Speed and Size, -C option
claim: Flex scanners use tables whose compression is configurable.
quote: A lone ‘-C’ specifies that the scanner tables should be compressed but neither equivalence classes nor meta-equivalence classes should be used.

claim: Some GCC lexer diagnostics depend on per-token lexer state.
quote: In both cases, whether a diagnostic is needed or not is dependent upon the lexer’s state.

locator: Lexing a token, whitespace and token positions
claim: GCC records the line and column of the first character of each token.
quote: Each token has its line and col variables set to the line and column of the first character of the token.

claim: Regular-expression alternation matches either operand language, and concatenation matches strings from one followed by strings from the other.
quote: Two regular expressions can be alternated or concatenated to form a new regular expression: if e1 matches s and e2 matches t, then e1|e2 matches s or t, and e1e2 matches st.

claim: An NFA accepts when some path consumes the input and reaches a matching state; unlabeled edges consume no input.
quote: An NFA matches an input string if there is some way it can read the string and follow arrows to a matching state. Sometimes it is convenient to let NFAs have arrows with no corresponding input character.

claim: Backreferences add expressive power beyond theoretical regular expressions.
quote: One common regular expression extension that does provide additional power is called backreferences.

claim: C postfix increment and decrement require a modifiable lvalue of real or pointer type.
quote: The operand of the postfix increment or decrement operator shall have atomic, qualified, or unqualified real or pointer type, and shall be a modifiable lvalue.

claim: C postfix increment yields the operand value and increments the operand as a side effect.
quote: The result of the postfix ++ operator is the value of the operand. As a side effect, the value of the operand object is incremented (that is, the value 1 of the appropriate type is added to it).

claim: C postfix decrement is analogous to postfix increment but subtracts one from the operand.
quote: The postfix -- operator is analogous to the postfix ++ operator, except that the value of the operand is decremented (that is, the value 1 of the appropriate type is subtracted from it).
